summary: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorization ($40.27, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, generally exempts Canadian citizens from a visa (CBP says those arriving by land or sea may generally visit for up to six months), and requires other visitors to obtain a B-1/B-2 visitor visa ($185), with an interview at a US embassy or consulate; citizens of the Marshall Islands and Micronesia, and Bahamians precleared in the Bahamas, also enter without a visa. Presidential proclamations of June and December 2025 suspend entry on visitor visas for citizens of the countries they list and for holders of Palestinian Authority travel documents, with limited exemptions.

visaTypes.name: ESTA — Electronic System for Travel Authorization

fee.notes: Payable online by card or PayPal. Covers tourism, business and transit under the Visa Waiver Program; only for nationals of VWP countries. The $40.27 is a $10.27 processing fee charged to every applicant, plus $30.00 if the application is approved (the $17 travel promotion fee and the $13 General Fund fee); applicants who are denied are charged only $10.27. DHS's fiscal year 2027 notice raises the fee to $40.62 from 16 October 2026.

stayDays.text: The Visa Waiver Program allows foreign nationals from certain countries to travel to the United States for business or pleasure, for stays of 90 days or less without obtaining a visa.

tips.text: Apply for ESTA on the official site esta.cbp.dhs.gov, where the fee is $40.27. A DHS notice in the Federal Register raises it to $40.62 from 16 October 2026.

DHS recommends applying for ESTA when you make your travel plans, and an approved travel authorization is required before boarding. Visa Waiver Program travelers entering by land also need an approved ESTA before they apply for admission (8 CFR 217.5), and CBP encourages them to apply at least 72 hours before arriving at a U.S. land port of entry.
The UK government says visa appointments at the US Embassy in London are limited and advises planning your application as far ahead of travel as possible.
The UK government says medical treatment in the US is expensive, that some hospitals ask non-US residents for a deposit on admission, and advises having adequate travel health insurance.

faq.question: What is ESTA and who needs it?
faq.answer: ESTA is the online travel authorization for the US Visa Waiver Program. Citizens of VWP countries (including the UK, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) must obtain it before boarding. It costs $40.27 — $40.62 from 16 October 2026 under DHS's fiscal year 2027 adjustment — is valid for 2 years (or until your passport expires) and allows stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How long can I stay in the US with ESTA?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days per visit, for tourism, business or transit. The ESTA site says that if you are admitted under the Visa Waiver Program you may not change or extend your status.

faq.question: How much does a US visitor visa cost?
faq.answer: The B-1/B-2 visitor visa application fee is $185. Depending on nationality, a reciprocity issuance fee may also be due when the visa is issued.

faq.question: Do Canadian citizens need ESTA or a visa for the US?
faq.answer: Canadian citizens generally do not need a visa: 8 CFR 212.1 says a visa is generally not required for Canadian citizens, except those in nonimmigrant visa categories E, K, S or V. ESTA is for citizens of the Visa Waiver Program countries listed by DHS, and Canada is not on that list. CBP says Canadian citizens traveling by land or sea may generally visit for up to six months.

faq.question: Is Romania in the US Visa Waiver Program?
faq.answer: No. DHS designated Romania for the Visa Waiver Program on 9 January 2025, paused implementation on 25 March 2025 and rescinded the designation on 2 May 2025, so Romanian citizens need a B-1/B-2 visitor visa ($185).
